# Marilla Cuthbert

## Appearance

Marilla Cuthbert is a tall, gaunt, and thin woman characterized by sharp angles rather than curves. She has dark hair streaked with gray that is tightly twisted into a small knot secured by two wire hairpins, and she is shorter in stature than [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md). Over time, her hair has grown grayer, and she occasionally exhibits a tired appearance.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER I. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Surprised P13](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0013), [v1 CHAPTER XXXI. ## Personality

Marilla Cuthbert is a sensible, self-contained woman of narrow experience and rigid conscience. Highly determined once her mind is made up, she possesses a crisp, curt demeanor and can become somewhat sarcastic when affected by headaches. Though she is stoic and reserved in expressing her affection, she strongly dislikes stinginess in children and scorns emotional weakness. She is also locally celebrated for her skill in making three-year-old homemade currant wine.

## History

Marilla Cuthbert lived at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) with her brother, [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md), carrying a lingering regret over a past quarrel with John Blythe and frequently suffering from headaches and eye pain. When she and [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) decided to adopt an orphan boy from [Nova Scotia](../codex/places.md#nova-scotia), a mix-up resulted in a young girl named [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) being brought to their home instead. Initially shocked and intent on returning [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), Marilla learned of the child's harsh past and felt deep pity for her, eventually convincing [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) that they should officially adopt and properly educate the girl. Over time, Marilla patiently managed Anne's dramatic mishaps—including a furious outburst at Mrs. [Rachel Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md), an accidental poisoning of the minister's wife's cake, and the accidental intoxication of [Diana Barry](../character/diana-barry.md) with homemade currant wine—while slowly growing deeply fond of the child. When Marilla falsely accused [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) of losing her prized amethyst brooch and forced a false confession, she realized her mistake after finding the brooch in her shawl and quickly apologized, sending [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) off to a school picnic. As [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) matured, Marilla supported her academic pursuits, allowing her to join the Queen's [Entrance](../codex/places.md#entrance) preparation class and later send her off to Queen's [Academy](../codex/places.md#academy). Following Matthew's sudden death from heart failure caused by the collapse of Abbey Bank, Marilla consulted an oculist, who warned her that she was going blind and had to give up reading and sewing to save her failing eyesight. Contemplating selling [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) due to her failing sight and grief, Marilla was saved from losing her home when [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) selflessly gave up her college scholarship to remain at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables), care for Marilla, and teach at the local [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) school.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER I. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Surprised P5](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0005), [v1 CHAPTER I. ## Quotes

> "I’d never dream of taking a girl to bring up. I wonder at Mrs. Alexander Spencer for doing it. But there, she wouldn’t shrink from adopting a whole orphan asylum if she took it into her head."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER I. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Surprised P29](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0029)

> "No. We want a boy to help Matthew on the farm. A girl would be of no use to us. Take off your hat. I’ll lay it and your bag on the hall table."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER III. Marilla Cuthbert Is Surprised P30](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0030)

> "Well, undress as quick as you can and go to bed. I’ll come back in a few minutes for the candle. I daren’t trust you to put it out yourself. You’d likely set the place on fire."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER III. Marilla Cuthbert Is Surprised P44](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0044)

> "I don’t feel as if I wanted any more children to look after than I’ve got at present. You’re problem enough in all conscience. What’s to be done with you I don’t know. Matthew is a most ridiculous man."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER IV. Morning at Green Gables P25](../source/v01-c04.md#nw-v01-c04-p0025)

> "We’re not talking about poetry, Anne—we are talking about saying your prayers. Don’t you know it’s a terrible wicked thing not to say your prayers every night? I’m afraid you are a very bad little girl."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER VII. Anne Says Her Prayers P11](../source/v01-c07.md#nw-v01-c07-p0011)

## Relationships

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--marilla-cuthbert.md)

Marilla becomes Anne's adoptive guardian after a mix-up brings the young girl to [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) instead of the expected boy. Though initially shocked and inclined to return her, Marilla decides to keep [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) after hearing about her hard life and witnessing the harsh alternative of sending her to Mrs. [Blewett](../character/peter-blewett.md). Over time, Marilla takes on the responsibility of educating and disciplining [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), guiding her through various childhood mishaps while gradually softening toward the imaginative girl.

- Parent of — adoptive parent / guardian raising her  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P89](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0089), [v1 CHAPTER XXVII. Vanity and Vexation of Spirit P3](../source/v01-c27.md#nw-v01-c27-p0003), [v1 CHAPTER XXIX. An Epoch in Anne’s Life P32](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0032), +1 more</sub>

### [Martin](../character/martin.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/marilla-cuthbert--martin.md)

[Martin](../character/martin.md) works at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) and drives for Marilla. His presence as a hired helper provides practical labor for the household, particularly around the time of Matthew's sudden death.

- Commands — drives for her and works at Green Gables  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XXXVII. The Reaper Whose Name Is Death P2](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0002), [v1 CHAPTER XXXVII. The Reaper Whose Name Is Death P28](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0028)</sub>

### [Rachel Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/marilla-cuthbert--rachel-lynde.md)

Mrs. [Rachel Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md) is Marilla's candid neighbor with whom she frequently consults and travels. Their relationship is marked by frank honesty, such as when [Rachel](../character/rachel-lynde.md) openly criticizes Marilla's choice to adopt a child and later insults Anne's appearance. Despite Rachel's blunt demeanor causing occasional conflict with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), Marilla maintains a close, long-standing bond with her, balancing community sociability with mutual support.

- Comrade of — traveling together to a political mass meeting in Charlottetown  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XVIII. Anne to the Rescue P1](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0001)</sub>
- Friend of — neighbors who consult each other for advice  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER I. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Surprised P12](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0012), [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P83](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0083), [v1 CHAPTER XXX. The Queen’s Class Is Organized P40](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0040), +1 more</sub>
